schema_note: No manifest-level schema: every entry names the component it is checked against, as '../openapi.json#/components/schemas/<Name>'. validate.py validates with the whole OpenAPI document as the root, so internal references resolve.
note: All values synthetic. PHI and leak guards: response-problem-echoes-input, response-validation-issue-with-message, response-problem-unknown-code. Proposed as OPENAPI_PHI_GUARDS (3) for tests/conformance. The readiness entry is the observability/v0 example itself, checked against ApiReadiness here too, so the two contracts cannot drift on the api case.
expectation_note: Pairs written 2026-10-05 by the architect WITHOUT a run: predictions until validate.py measures them.

valid.note: POST /v1/channels or /versions: authored document (no metadata.version), git origin with commit and path
expected_current_version null: deploy only if nothing is deployed
to_version defaults to the previously published version
Undeploy: version null; failed carries failure_code
Paths and keywords or rule names only; a control-plane warning code
Management mode and profile per environment
Cross-contract: the observability api readiness example must also satisfy the OpenAPI response schema

invalid.violates: a git origin names its commit and path
no force flag or any other unknown field: strict producers
rollback requires expected_current_version, so a double rollback fails instead of going two versions back
a problem never echoes the request (invariant 6; a URL can carry a token)
a validation issue is json_path plus keyword; the jsonschema message embeds the failing value
an undeploy publishes a tombstone, so version is null
published means committed to _tb.<env>.channels, and says when
problem codes are a closed list; a library exception name is not one
spec_sha256 is 64 lowercase hex, no prefix
